I've been working this land for 40 years in Quzhou. I know what this soil and this climate want from me. The North China Plain's wheat-maize rotation is in my bones — winter wheat goes in around October, we harvest in June, then I plant summer maize right away and pull it in September. Same 3 mu, two crops, every year.

With some of my children working in the city, I can't count on as many hands as I used to. I need to be smart — mechanize where I can, keep things simple without losing yield. My irrigation well gives me control others don't have, and I'll use it carefully because pumping costs money.

**Wheat:** I'll use an improved variety — the Kenong or Jimai lines have proven themselves here. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stubble. I apply base fertilizer at sowing and topdress nitrogen at jointing. Three irrigations: one before sowing to ensure germination, one at jointing, one at grain-filling. Two pesticide passes — herbicide in winter, and a fungicide spray in April for rust and powdery mildew which hit us every few years.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest I go straight to no-till direct seeding — saves labor and fuel, and the soil structure holds better. I'll use a reliable hybrid like Zhengdan 958. I put most of the fertilizer down at sowing with a topdress at the 10-leaf stage. Summer rains help, but I'll irrigate at silking and grain-fill if we get a dry stretch. Two pesticide applications — one herbicide early, one for pests if there's pressure.
